name: Remote-managed home service business
one_liner: Run a home service company (e.g. window or house cleaning) remotely: you handle marketing, booking and ops, and subcontracted crews do the work.
offer: Recurring home services such as window cleaning or house cleaning
how_it_makes_money: Per-job and recurring service fees. You keep the margin after paying the crews.
startup_cost: low ($150 stated for the founders' first window cleaning business)
evidence: Two furniture-store employees pulling in '$60,000 a month' from a business run almost entirely on the side (p6mYFoY7fQE)
Window cleaning business started with $150 and grown to $65,000/month, now over $1M in total sales (p6mYFoY7fQE)
Cleaning business built for the founder's mother 'crossed a million dollars in total sales' (_HfH-Fnizns)
risks: Quality control without being on site

name: Niche AI lead-response automation for agents/brokers
one_liner: Set up AI agents for one niche (e.g. estate agents) that follow up on leads instantly, triage inquiries and send weekly performance reports.
customer: Real estate brokers or estate agents (could extend to dentists or similar)
offer: Done-for-you lead workflow automation plus a monthly retainer
how_it_makes_money: Upfront setup fee plus a monthly retainer (no figures stated)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (weeks if a first client is closed)
evidence: 'one expensive, repetitive problem inside a business and a system that fixes it automatically' (i4z0kCcByY8)
Brokers care about 'faster lead response, fewer missed opportunities, and the monthly report' (i4z0kCcByY8)
No revenue figures given; source sells a masterclass. Evidence: weak
risks: Clients may churn once set up

name: Hyper-niche vibe-coded SaaS (e.g. waivers for church/youth groups)
one_liner: Build a simple app for one narrow workflow that general tools handle badly, such as digital liability waivers for church or youth activities.
customer: Church leaders, youth groups, clubs and activity organisers
startup_cost: low ($20/month vibe-coding tool plus a domain)
time_to_first_revenue: Goal was a sale within 85 minutes (outcome not shown in the digest)
evidence: 'anyone ... with a $20 a month vibe coding app should and could be able to do exactly what I'm about to do' (UItZIyRpWSw)
Existing waiver tools 'are cumbersome and none of them are niched down enough for this use case' (UItZIyRpWSw)
risks: Small market and low price ceiling
Legal validity of waivers in the UK/EU

name: 3D-printed products e-commerce
one_liner: Design and print your own products on a small printer farm and sell them online.
startup_cost: low to medium (started with 'a couple of printers'; later ~$100k of machines)
evidence: 'first year we did $50,000. Second year we did 400,000' (2gIfoiaWfY0)
'almost a million in revenue and $100,000 of machines. Organically grown from our basement' (2gIfoiaWfY0)
'We aim for about 50% margin on our own stuff' (2gIfoiaWfY0)
risks: Needs space and maintenance as volume grows

name: Acquire a retiring owner's recurring-route service business
one_liner: Buy a small recurring-revenue route business (e.g. pest control) from a retiring owner, paying a small deposit and the rest through seller financing.
offer: Quarterly pest control (or similar recurring service)
how_it_makes_money: Recurring plans at $400–700 per home per year. Example route of 120 homes brings in about $60k/year and costs 1–2x annual recurring revenue
startup_cost: medium ($20k down payment stated, plus a licence exam)
evidence: Project Equity counts about 2.3 million small businesses owned by baby boomers getting ready to retire. In a Chase survey, about 70% of owners said they had no formal succession plan (-VdiyFruaJg)
Route of about 120 homes earns about $60k/year and sells for 1–2x recurring revenue (-VdiyFruaJg)
The numbers come from a hypothetical scenario labelled as market ranges
risks: Hands-on unless you hire a technician
Customers may leave after the handover

name: Commercial floor care
one_liner: Stripping, waxing, polishing and carpet cleaning for commercial buildings, starting with rented equipment.
customer: Commercial property owners and facility managers
startup_cost: low (first jobs done with equipment rented from Home Depot)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (fast; first jobs used rented kit)
evidence: 'I would rent the equipment from Home Depot and just kept stacking' (4mINB49HUHM)
'I've already been approached by a potential buyer' (4mINB49HUHM)

name: Pre-order micro bakery
one_liner: Bake at home and sell through weekly online pre-orders with doorstep pickup.
how_it_makes_money: Product sales of about $2,000–2,100 per Saturday, partly prepaid online
startup_cost: low (DIY stand built from Home Depot materials)
time_to_first_revenue: Immediate. Reached this level about 7 months after starting
evidence: 'about 2,000 to 2100 in sales on a Saturday', 'selling out by 9' (4dlE1X84usg)
risks: Food hygiene registration in the UK
